title: Word Problems Within 100
intro: Separate understanding the story from carrying out the calculation.
html:
Teaching notes for parents and teachers

How to teach it

Ask the student to sketch what happens to the collection. Once the equation matches the story, support the calculation with tens and ones.

Example to work through together

Use the model below as you explain the example. Have your student point to the quantities as you discuss them.

First collection: 38 counters.

New counters: 27.

38 + 27 = 65

38 + 20 = 58, then 58 + 7 = 65.

52 − 10 = 42
42 − 8 = 34
34 + 18 = 52

The last equation checks that the remaining counters and the given-away counters rebuild the starting collection.

Ask your student

What happened to the starting collection?

If your student needs help

If the equation is right but the calculation is wrong, work on the place-value step without changing the student's model of the story.
